Thomas and Mina nodded in quiet agreement. They were standing together in a hostile city, backed into a corner with threats closing in from all sides. Looking ahead at the cold stone corridors beneath the mountain, Lucas knew the true crucible was already upon them.

Chapter 16 - Part 4: The Obsidian Cipher

Penta-cres, Borin 1772 HSC — The Causal Genesis

The ambient temperature plummeted, plunging the party into a suffocating chill as they descended deep into the forgotten bedrock beneath Brum’korath. The faint, volatile radiation of the dwarven aether-lamps cast jagged, shifting shadows across ancient cyclopean masonry. These tunnels were raw, primal scars carved into the lithosphere, forged by an archaic civilization that defied modern terrestrial engineering.

Lucas walked at the vanguard, his calculating mind registering an archaic, heavy pressure watching them from the surrounding stone. Mina trailed closely, her shoulder brushing against the unyielding, tectonic bulwark of Thomas. Torgar led the descent, utilizing the fragmented archives surrendered by Dira, his heavy boots grinding a slow rhythm into the dust.

“These corridors predate the foundation of Brum’korath,” Torgar murmured, his voice a low vibration respectful of the crushing, sterile silence. “The texts debate their genesis—some attribute the masonry to the Ancients, others insist the first Sent Ones carved this path seeking the absolute truth. The history is buried in the dark.”

Mina halted, her green eyes locking onto a sprawling relief etched deep into the cavern wall. It depicted towering, humanoid figures raising their hands toward an erupting cosmic anomaly, a spiraling vortex of fractured stars. She traced the jagged lines with a gloved finger. A restless, violent surge rippled across her skin, the raw creation energy in her blood syncing with the ancient carving.

“Can you feel that?” Mina asked, her fingers hovering millimeters above the stone, her eyes tracing the jagged seams. “In the walls... the air. It’s like the whole corridor is humming right under our skin.”

Lucas leaned in, extending his consciousness into the surrounding stone. The sensory feedback struck his neural pathways with the sharp, sterile clarity of an active circuit. He felt the bedrock vibrating with an immense, coiled tension. A subterranean current flowed through the crystalline lattice of the granite, weaving microscopic filaments of power through every fracture and joint in the masonry. As his mind traced the intricate etchings, the chilling logic of the architecture snapped into focus: the reliefs functioned as intricate geometric circuitry. The entire corridor operated as a calibrated load-bearing matrix, routing an enormous reservoir of pressurized power through the stone to sustain the structural integrity of the vault—and to act as a suffocating quarantine seal, actively suppressing whatever rested in the deep core to keep the dormant force from rupturing the mountain crust.

“The air and the stone are saturated,” Lucas stated, pulling his focus back behind his mental firewalls as the pressure registered in his teeth. “This entire vault is an active containment matrix.”

Thomas shifted his stance, his heavy boots grinding against the loose gravel. “A what now?” he grunted, casting a flat, unimpressed look at the glowing stonework. “Speak plain, Lucas. Are we walking into a fortress, or is the ceiling about to cave in on our heads?”

“A pressure lock,” Lucas clarified, his voice tight with clinical focus. “The stonework is engineered to cage a volatile power source and keep the bedrock from buckling under the strain.”

Thomas folded his arms, his dark eyes narrowing as he assessed the reinforced passage with a defender's instinct. “A pressure lock... or a deadbolt built to keep anyone from walking inside?”

“Both,” Lucas replied, his synthesis mind tracing the dual pathways of the conduit. “The architecture is bi-directional. It suffocates the power locked in the core, and it erects a lethal barrier against anything attempting to breach the perimeter from the outside.”

They advanced until the corridor terminated abruptly against a massive, monolithic slab of dark iron. The door was choked with dense, geometric runes that pulsed faintly with a dormant, unnatural light.

Mina halted before the threshold, her brow furrowing as she studied the glowing alloy. “This door feels way weirder than the carvings back there,” she murmured, her fingers curling into fists as her pulse quickened. “It’s humming... like it’s pulling right at me. I can feel it in my blood.”

Lucas stepped up beside her, extending a clinical probe of his consciousness toward the monolithic slab. He threaded his mind directly into the dense lock matrix woven across the iron. The sensory feedback struck his neural pathways with an uncanny familiarity. The rhythmic wavelength flowing through the runes mirrored the exact cadence of Mina’s vital current—the untamed warmth pulsing through her blood. The harmonic resonance washed over the frayed circuits of his overtaxed mind, pacifying the chronic tension in his skull with a soothing, profound clarity.

Beneath that living cadence, his consciousness struck a mirrored, interlocking channel—a sterile, geometric groove calibrated to the exact architecture of his own mind. The lock housed a secondary circuit waiting for his chilling, focused spark, keyed directly to his unique cognitive signature.

Bypassing his compulsive need to calculate every variable, Lucas acted on pure impulse. He pressed his fingers against the dark alloy and channeled a steady pulse of his power into the stone. The reaction was instantaneous. The iron slab drank the cold current, illuminating a faint line of pale-blue light along the geometric seams as the door's dormant circuitry stirred in direct response to his touch.

It’s keyed to both of us, Lucas projected across their bond, his mental voice quiet with disbelief. The lock is pulsing with your exact frequency, and mine. It feels just like your warmth, Mina... it's actually quieting the static in my head.

Mina glanced at him, surprise sparking in her green eyes, before turning her gaze back to the dark iron. She stepped forward and pressed her palm flat against the cold metal.

At first, the slab remained completely inert and motionless. Beneath her skin, she registered only a deep, subterranean vibration—a slow, rhythmic hum pulsing through the alloy that mirrored the cadence of her own heart.

Lucas stepped closer, resting a gentle hand on her shoulder, his voice quiet, calm, and reassuring. “It's just asleep,” he said softly, meeting her eyes to help settle her racing pulse. “The door recognizes you, Mina. It just needs you to wake it up. Take a breath, and let your energy flow gently into the iron.”

Mina hesitated, a knot of dread tightening in her stomach. The memory of the wild, suffocating thicket she had accidentally ruptured back at the Bastion flashed in her mind. Her creation magic was an untamed, volatile current, notoriously difficult to meter. “Lucas, I don't know how to throttle it,” she whispered, her fingers trembling against the cold iron. “Every time I let that current loose, it runs away from me.”

Before Lucas could answer, the Justice Hall envoy stepped forward from the escort detail, his slate ledger clutched under his arm as he stared at the pulsating runes with deep unease. “Are you certain it is safe to breach that seal?” the dwarven magistrate asked, his voice hushed and cautious. “I have audited centuries of dwarven and terrestrial records. Glyphs of this geometry exist entirely outside the recorded history of Hybris. Whatever engineered this slab predates our oldest archives.”

Taking a measured step backward, the envoy signaled to the two armored sentinels flanking the passage. “Secure the threshold. Keep your pikes leveled and be prepared for anything.”

Lucas maintained his mental scan of the door's pathways, his voice steady and clinical. “The aetheric flow carries zero defensive hostility. The conduits route current exclusively into the release relays. It functions strictly as a lock.”

Mina ignored the bureaucrat, locking her eyes onto Lucas. In his dark gaze, she found an unyielding, steady clarity.

I'm right here, Lucas projected across their bond, his presence wrapping gently around hers to steady her racing heart. Don’t be afraid of the power, Mina. Just let it flow into the iron. I'm holding onto you—I won't let you lose control.

Reassured by his mental presence, Mina closed her eyes and released the internal brakes on her power.

The raw creation energy surged from her chest like an unleashed torrent. Lacking the fine calibration to meter the feed, her output violently oversaturated the circuit, dumping an enormous excess of vitality straight into the surrounding bedrock.

The cavern floor shuddered violently. Jagged fissures tore through the flagstones as ancient, dormant root systems gorged on her overflowing current. Pale, thick subterranean vines erupted from the cracked bedrock, twisting aggressively up the massive doorframe. Dense clusters of bioluminescent fungi ruptured from the seams in the stone, swelling into bloated caps that burst, showering the corridor in clouds of glowing, shimmering spores. The sudden, feral eruption of life forced the startled dwarven guards to stumble backward, coughing against the drifting dust.

For several agonizing seconds, the iron slab groaned under the crushing, continuous deluge of power. Lacking the calibration to regulate the flow, she poured far more energy into the lock than the ancient design required. Finally, the dense runes across the iron flared into a brilliant, blinding white-blue radiance as the ancient matrix became fully saturated.

A violent pulse of raw energy arced from the stone, forcing a sharp intake of breath into Mina's lungs. The stone tunnel vanished from her sight, stranding her in an absolute, lightless void where a singular, blinding star burned with terrifying intensity. A deep voice resonated directly inside her skull.

The trajectory is locked, but you forge the steps.

“Mina!” Lucas’s voice shattered the vision. His hands caught her trembling shoulders, the physical contact instantly severing the trance and pulling her back into reality. She staggered backward, gasping for air as her boots scraped against the overgrown flagstones, leaning heavily into Lucas's chest.

Before them, the ancient mechanism completed its release. With a deafening, grinding groan of stone on iron, the massive slab split down the center, sliding smoothly into the bedrock recesses to exhale a freezing rush of centuries-old, stagnant air.

Mina pressed a shaking hand against her forehead, her green eyes wide as she stared into the dark opening. “Did you hear that?” she whispered, her breath catching as the echo of the voice lingered in her mind.

“Hear what?” Lucas asked, his dark eyes scanning the newly opened breach while his grip stayed firm on her arm to keep her upright.

“A voice,” she breathed, turning to look at him. “Inside my head. It said the trajectory is locked, but we forge the steps.”

The sprawling chamber beyond dwarfed the antechamber. Colossal murals documented ancient, apocalyptic wars. At the dead center of the room, a lone stone pedestal housed a jagged obsidian shard. The artifact hummed with a chilling, cold stillness that gnawed at their instincts.

Mina approached the dais, her green eyes scanning the towering figures carved across the wall. The reliefs depicted four distinct, cataclysmic heralds descending alongside an invading armada from the stars, each bearing the mark of an elemental devastation—earth, wind, flame, and water.

“The Four Calamities,” Dira gasped, rushing forward, her trembling fingers hovering over the runic inscriptions beneath the relief. Her scholar's gaze darted across the archaic glyphs, piece by piece unraveling the centuries-old error. “Our oldest tablets spoke of the *Four Calamities of the Deep*—our translators treated them as mythological metaphors for planetary disasters: seismic fractures, volcanic eruptions, oceanic deluges, and hurricane gales. They assumed our ancestors were describing raw geological wrath.” Her voice dropped to a terrified whisper. “They completely mistranslated the archaic syntax. The texts were documenting four engineered siege weapons—biological titans designed to tear a world apart element by element.”

“And the Disciple in the square was only the first,” Mina murmured, her breath catching as the sheer scale of the war settled into her chest. “There are three more heralds out there. And an entire armada waiting behind them.”

Torgar stepped toward the central pedestal, his mace lowering as a scholar’s reverence broke through his hardened exterior. He leaned in, his thick, calloused fingers hovering millimeters above the floating obsidian shard, his dark eyes analyzing the strange, seamless geometry of the dark metal. “By the foundations of the stone...” Torgar breathed, awe hollowing his voice. “The shifting treasure from the First Scraps... the oldest Nythari fragments spoke of a sacred tool forged from fluid stone, an artifact capable of taking many forms. The clerics treated the texts as parables, yet the alloy rests here before us, perfectly intact.”

“It’s immaculate,” Dira whispered, stepping past him, her scholar's gaze completely transfixed by the dark metal. “Centuries buried in the deep earth, yet the surface repels every speck of grime and dust. It rests here in absolute purity.”

Mesmerized by the ancient craft, she reached out on pure impulse, her trembling fingertips brushing against the edge of the floating shard.

The reaction was violent and instantaneous. A sharp pulse of crimson force detonated from the dais, hurling Dira backward onto the flagstones. The unauthorized touch tripped the sanctum's ancient security relays, and the chamber’s dormant defense grid roared to life.

The towering, petrified statues of ancient Sent Ones lining the chamber shed their stillness. Eight colossal monoliths of black basalt, standing ten feet tall with severe, faceless visors, ground into motion. Centuried stone sheared against stone as they stepped down from their pedestals, shedding avalanches of dust and pulverized mortar from their broad, geometric shoulders. Deep fissures carved across their torsos ignited, channeling a pressurized, toxic-green aetheric current that bled through their eye-slits like radioactive fire. In their massive stone hands, nine-foot polearms and jagged executioner blades—carved seamlessly from the same unyielding bedrock—dragged across the flagstones with an ear-splitting, metallic shriek.

A subterranean acoustic frequency vibrated straight through the marrow of their bones, grinding from the very masonry: The sanctum is breached. The purge begins.

Behind them, the massive iron slab that Mina had just breached violently snapped back into motion. With a concussive, deafening boom that shook the dust from the ceiling, the two halves slammed shut, the dense runic glyphs flaring crimson as ancient mechanical deadbolts locked into the bedrock. The trap was absolute. Sealed within the suffocating kill-box—Lucas, Mina, Thomas, Torgar, Dira, the pale Justice Hall envoy, and the two trembling militia sentinels—the party was completely severed from the corridor behind them.

The atmospheric pressure compressed violently as the eight basalt constructs advanced, moving with the crushing, rhythmic cadence of an automated execution line. At every articulation—knees, shoulders, and elbows—the dark mineral dissolved into an uncanny, fluid state. Seams of viscous obsidian churned and stretched like molten black glass, flowing with an unnerving, liquid grace before instantly hardening into petrified stone with each heavy impact. They possessed zero biological hesitation, their heavy footfalls fracturing the floor as they closed the perimeter with suffocating precision.

Thomas planted his heavy boots into the stone, bracing his shield against the descending strike of the first basalt construct. The massive stone axe slammed into his bulwark with tectonic force, sending a concussive shockwave through his forearms, but his rooted foundation absorbed the crushing inertia. Beside him, the second statue swept a jagged polearm in a low, shearing arc. Torgar lunged forward, his heavy mace intercepting the blow with a shower of sparks that gouged shallow fissures into the construct's basalt forearm.

Planting his boots firmly against the flagstones, Torgar began a deep, guttural chant—singing an ancient dwarven earth canticle in low, reverberating frequencies. The acoustic resonance ground through the bedrock, washing over every defender in the room. The terrestrial magic took hold, anchoring their footing with unyielding traction and reinforcing their skin and armor with the dense resilience of stone.

Across the open floor, the third and fourth constructs converged on Mina in a coordinated pincer strike, their heavy double-edged blades slashing the air from opposite flanks. Mina leaned into her untamed heat, ducking beneath the first descending blade in a fluid blur. Riding the slipstream, she vaulted off the flat of the second weapon, twisting mid-air with feral grace. She drove a concentrated, concussive heel-strike directly into the third construct’s fluid obsidian knee. The viscous black glass churned under the impact, forcing the ten-foot titan to buckle hard against the floor.

Dira scrambled backward, her breath coming in ragged gasps as she sought cover. The circular hall offered minimal shelter, its vast curved perimeter rising straight into a soaring square dome with completely exposed flagstones. She pressed her spine flat against the bare stone wall at the edge of the chamber, clutching her leather ledger to her chest.

The fifth construct drove a massive stone spear straight toward the two militia guards near Dira. The sentinels crossed their pikes to deflect the thrust, but the sheer blunt force shattered the shaft of the first guard's weapon. The stone spearhead slammed across his breastplate, lifting him off his boots and throwing him violently against the curved wall. The guard struck the masonry with a heavy crack, spitting blood and clutching his fractured ribs, but he gritted his teeth and remained on his feet, drawing his heavy sidearm blade with trembling hands.

The sixth construct lunged to crush the wounded guard and the cornered scribe, its massive basalt fist raised like a falling boulder.

The Justice Hall envoy dropped his slate ledger, stepping seamlessly into the strike zone. Stripping away his bureaucratic demeanor, the dwarven magistrate revealed a master's command of barehanded stone-fist martial arts. As the colossal stone fist plummeted, the envoy pivoted on his heels, executing an open-palm deflection along the construct's forearm. Shifting his body weight with lethal precision, he drove a concentrated, vibration-infused palm strike directly into the construct's fluid obsidian elbow. The viscous black glass ruptured under the concussive focus, dislocating the stone articulation and sending the construct reeling off balance.

The seventh and eighth constructs advanced directly on the center of the hall, their nine-foot polearms sweeping in a lethal scissor formation to eradicate the core.

Lucas stepped forward, raising both hands to project sterile, geometric barriers of force into the air. The descending blade of the seventh construct collided with his invisible shield, rattling the focus in his skull, while the eighth construct slammed its weapon into the floorboards, sending stone shrapnel skittering across the room.

Holding the barrier steady, Lucas narrowed his focus, actively probing the aetheric currents animating the constructs. He threaded his consciousness into the toxic-green fire burning in the seventh statue's chest. Tracing the frequency inward, his synthesis mind mapped a microscopic energy conduit feeding the stone. The current did not originate from the construct's own core; it was being actively drawn through a subterranean tether anchored directly to the jagged obsidian shard floating above the central dais.

“The shard is their power source!” Lucas shouted over the grinding stone. “It’s feeding the current to every single construct in this room!”

With the constructs recovering for a coordinated second strike, Lucas dropped his defensive barrier and sprinted for the dais, sliding low across the flagstones beneath the sweeping arc of a stone spear. He thrust his hand toward the obsidian shard.

The artifact reacted violently to his touch. The jagged stone liquefied, wrapping around his wrist like a living vine before hardening into a sleek, dark band. A blinding shock tore through his nervous system as an intense surge of cold energy flooded his mind, scouring his thoughts for a fraction of a second before abruptly collapsing.

The metallic wristband ceased all active feedback. The surging current vanished, the glow extinguished, and the alloy settled into inert stone, binding flush against his skin in absolute stillness.

Yet, the initial contact was enough to sever the room's arcane current.

The towering sentinels halted mid-strike, their toxic-green gaze dying into cold, lifeless stone. With the aetheric current instantly severed, the fluid obsidian across their joints petrified on the spot, locking their colossal frames into an eerie gallery of arrested momentum. The frozen postures formed a bizarre, theatrical collision of forms: the construct before Thomas stood locked in a monumental, epic tableau, its heavy stone axe hovering inches above his shield; the statue Mina had struck remained suspended in a strange, poetic arch like a dancer caught mid-pirouette; while near the wall, the sentinel the envoy had dislocated stood frozen in a clumsy, asymmetrical crouch, its head tilted and one stone arm dangling at a comically baffled angle over Dira. Another remained teetering on the edge of a single foot, paralyzed in an awkward lurch that mocked its towering size.

The violent friction evaporated in a heartbeat, plunging the cavernous dome back into absolute, echoing silence.

Lucas stood over the pedestal, his chest heaving as he stared down at the dark metal fused seamlessly to his wrist. It rested flush against his flesh, radiating a heavy, cold stillness.

Mina stepped up to the dais, her green eyes wide as she reached out to inspect the seamless band. “Lucas... can you pry it off?”

Lucas pulled at the edge of the dark alloy, but the metal remained immovable, bonded flush to his skin like a second layer of bone. “It's completely locked,” Lucas rasped, catching his breath as his fingers traced the seamless surface. “Touching it cut the circuit to the statues, but that's all.”

The fragments of an ancient puzzle were slowly assembling across the dark stone—the murals of the Four Calamities, the fluid alloy of the relic, and the uncanny resonance woven into the masonry. Yet every answer unearthed in the deep earth only multiplied the questions, leaving them suspended in the quiet of a labyrinth they were only beginning to comprehend.

Chapter 16 - Part 5: Unfinished Threads

Penta-cres, Borin 1772 HSC — The Causal Genesis

The air inside the dark corridor hung heavy and suffocating. Every footfall echoed off the ancient stone, cutting through the silence as they retraced their steps. Shadows warped along the carved walls, twisted by the pale, cold light radiating from the metal band fused around Lucas’s wrist. The dim gleam traced the contours of the rock, sharpening the severe, foreboding shapes of the forgotten architecture.

“Are you certain of the path?” Torgar rumbled, the heavy shaft of his war-axe resting across his broad, armored shoulder as his dark eyes swept the dark.

“We need to understand what these things are doing to us,” Lucas replied, his voice flat with exhaustion as he looked down at the band encircling his wrist. The metal rested flush against his skin, cold and unnervingly still, yet humming with a faint pulse that vibrated straight through his bones.

Mina pressed ahead of the group, her jaw set with quiet resolve. She halted before the threshold of the second artifact chamber. The air here was freezing and stale, heavy with a lingering dread. The room was arranged identically to the first: cold, solemn, and centered around a raised pedestal of black bedrock where the second relic rested in absolute silence.

A restless, untamed heat coiled in Mina’s muscles, driving her across the threshold without a heartbeat of hesitation.

“Mina, wait—” Thomas began, stepping forward to catch her shoulder.

Her fingers closed over the artifact.

The relic reacted instantly. A sudden, blinding flare erupted from the pedestal, washing the stone chamber in brilliant, white-blue light. Mina gasped, her spine arching as the raw current surged up her arm. The metallic mass liquefied, flowing down her frame in a serpentine blur of liquid silver before coiling tightly around her ankle. The alloy solidified into a seamless, cold band, clamping shut with a sharp click. Mina stumbled backward, throwing her hands out to balance herself against the rough stone pedestal, her breath tearing through her throat.

“It’s... cold,” she murmured, lifting her foot and rotating her ankle. A strange, sharp tension vibrated beneath her skin—a rigid, chilling muzzle clamped directly over her rushing vitality. Her voice carried a quiet mixture of awe and unease.

Dira moved swiftly to her side, her blue eyes wide with terror as she knelt to inspect the binding. “Are you hurt? Can you feel your leg?”

“No,” Mina replied, shaking her head as she pushed herself upright. “I’m in one piece. It’s just... there.” She turned her green eyes toward Lucas, holding his gaze. “It matches yours.”

Lucas gave a tight nod, his lips pressed into a thin line. “We find the third one.”

The third chamber loomed at the end of the descending corridor, its entrance radiating an even heavier, monolithic presence. The ancient glyphs etched into the stone doorframe pulsed with a faint, steady glow as they crossed the threshold. The silence inside was absolute, pressing against their ears like deep water.

At the center of the chamber, resting upon a weathered stone dais, lay the final relic—deceptively simple, a geometric fragment of unyielding dark alloy.

“Your turn,” Mina murmured softly, her breath visible in the freezing air as she glanced at Thomas.

Thomas hesitated. He stood before the dais, his massive hand hovering inches above the cold metal. He threw a quick glance back toward Lucas. Lucas met his eyes, offering a firm nod. Thomas drew a deep, ragged breath and closed his calloused fingers around the relic.

The moment his skin made contact, a violent shockwave tore through the chamber.

A blinding flash of energy ruptured outward, rattling the stones in the ceiling. Thomas cried out—a harsh, guttural roar of agony. The relic liquefied and snapped around his right wrist, compressing with crushing force until the metal bit deep into his flesh. Thomas stumbled backward, his heavy boots carving trenches into the dust. He dropped to one knee, clutching his skull with both hands as a thick stream of dark blood spilled rapidly from his nose.

“Thomas!” Mina and Lucas shouted in unison, lunging across the flagstones to catch him.

“I’m fine,” Thomas grunted through clenched teeth, his hands clamping over his temples as blood dripped onto the stone. “Just... blinding pain in my head. Give me a second.”

Dira dropped to her knees beside him, her hands trembling as she reached for the blood smearing his jawline. “You’re bleeding from your nose! Something is tearing into your head!”

Lucas reached straight into his friend's mind. Under normal conditions, Thomas’s thoughts were an impenetrable silence, an unyielding wall where no magic could take root. But as Lucas brushed the boundary, a sickening, freezing shock hit him. He gasped, tearing his mind away as if burned.

“What did you see?” Mina demanded, her hands tightening on Thomas’s shoulder.

“Something is tearing through his head,” Lucas said, his voice shaking. “The relic isn't just binding to him—it's forcing its way into his mind, rewriting his thoughts from the inside out.”

The group exchanged horrified, tense glances. The air grew brittle.

“Rewriting his mind? What is it doing to him?” Torgar demanded, his grip tightening white-knuckled around the haft of his battle-axe.

“I don't know,” Lucas admitted, his breath catching. “It's completely different from what it did to Mina or me. Thomas doesn't have magic, so the relic is forcing its way straight into his flesh and blood. The strain is tearing him apart.”

Dira scrambled backward in sheer panic. “We have to get it off him!”

They moved instantly. Mina anchored Thomas’s arm, channeling her untamed strength to pull at the silver band, while Dira wedged an iron pry-tool beneath the seam. Torgar added his massive, dwarven leverage, hauling against the metal until the stone beneath their boots groans under the strain. The band remained absolute. It rested flush against Thomas’s wrist, an immovable, seamless ring of foreign alloy that completely ignored their physical force.

After several agonizing minutes of futile exertion, Thomas shoved their hands away. His face was deathly pale, blood matting his upper lip, but his dark eyes burned with fierce, unyielding determination.

“Enough,” Thomas grumbled, his voice dropping into a flat, grounded tone. “The pain is backing off. It’s just a vicious headache.”

Mina’s brow furrowed, her pulse racing with protective anger. “You’re bleeding from your nose, Thomas. You're hurt.”

“We don’t have time to argue,” Thomas snapped, a sudden, harsh edge cutting through his voice that startled them all. He immediately winced, pressing a hand against his temple as he caught his breath. “Sorry. My head is pounding. Let's just find whatever is in this room and get out.”

The party turned back to the surrounding walls with a heightened, desperate urgency. Lucas moved along the perimeter of the third chamber, his fingers tracing the cold, jagged grooves of the glyphs carved deep into the granite. The rough stone felt freezing beneath his touch, yet a strange, faint hum vibrated against his fingertips.

“The history carved here is broken,” Lucas said, tracing the jagged grooves in the stone. “It speaks of the Sent Ones, the Unbound, and some ancient duty to guard the mountain. But whole sections have been chiseled away. Someone deliberately erased half the story.”

“Or truths our ancestors weren't meant to understand,” Dira murmured, her voice tight as she sketched the symbols into her leather ledger.

Torgar grunted, his gaze tracking the faint lines in the rock. “Whoever forged these relics, we are meddling with powers that could bring this whole mountain down.”

“We need more answers,” Mina said, stepping beside Lucas. “Or someone who can actually read the old tongues.”

“And what happens when our time runs out?” Thomas asked, leaning heavily against the stone. His voice was steady, but Lucas could hear the raw strain behind it.

The group fell into a heavy silence. The three metallic bands—locked seamlessly to their wrists and ankle—hummed with a faint, unified pulse, a permanent physical reminder of the trap closing around them.

“We head back to the surface,” Lucas said, breaking the quiet. “We take what Dira copied back to the Bastion and figure out our next move before this place triggers another trap.”

Reluctantly, the group complied, turning their backs on the third pedestal and retreating into the dark corridors. The physical weight of the relics—and the terrifying unknowns governing their function—shadowed every step like an executioner's blade.

The flickering, amber light of the oil torches cast long, trembling silhouettes across the stone walls as the party continued their survey of the deeper archival halls connecting the chambers. After the brutal confrontations of the preceding days—the catastrophic descent of the Disciple of Earth, the violent trial of Goldar, and the irreversible bonding of the relics—the fugitives had grown accustomed to the crushing gravity of the unknown. Yet, as they ventured deeper into the forgotten roots of the temple, the atmospheric pressure of impending collapse mounted with every yard.

The ancient stonework around them groaned softly, a low subterranean vibration carrying the whispers of an era erased from terrestrial memory. Every corner of the vaulted corridors held data just out of reach. Despite their bone-deep exhaustion, Lucas, Mina, and Thomas remained driven by pure survival. This was no longer merely about evading the World Police or the dwarven militia; it was about deciphering their assigned roles in a cosmic war they had never agreed to fight.

Thomas walked slightly apart from the others, his fingers resting against the cold metal band on his wrist. It was completely seamless, yet it carried an unnatural weight that threw off his balance. The blinding agony in his head had faded to a dull, grinding throb, but something had fundamentally shifted behind his eyes. The metal hummed quietly beneath his pulse, and Thomas knew with chilling certainty that it wasn't done with him.

Mina watched him closely, her green eyes sharp with concern. “How are you holding up?” she asked softly, keeping her voice low in the quiet hall.

“I’m managing,” he replied slowly, though the exhaustion in his eyes betrayed him. “The metal... it’s doing something to my head. Like it’s sorting through my thoughts and shifting things around. It doesn’t hurt anymore, but it feels completely foreign.”

Lucas stepped away from a wall carving, turning to his friend. “What do you mean?” Lucas asked, concern sharpening his voice. “What is it changing?”

“I don't know how to explain it,” Thomas replied, staring down at the band. “It feels like someone else is rifling through my memories, rearranging how I react to things. It’s not breaking anything, but it’s changing me.”

Mina exchanged a troubled look with Lucas. Both of them had felt the freezing, heavy weight of their own relics, but neither had endured the strange invasion quietly reshaping Thomas’s mind. The truth was settling in: these artifacts were not ordinary dwarven treasures. They were ancient, terrifying pieces of a forgotten age, bound to a past none of them understood.

“We'll figure it out,” Lucas promised, his tone steadying. “We'll find a way to stop it.”

Thomas shook his head, forcing his posture straight. “We don't have time to worry about me right now. We need answers about what's coming, and we need them fast.”

The party resumed their examination of the sprawling reliefs etched into the subterranean stone. Despite the suffocating dread in his chest, Lucas traced the geometric lines with clinical fascination. The carvings pulsed with a microscopic current, as if waiting for a specific, anomalous spark to ignite their dormant records.

“The reliefs tell a continuous story,” Lucas murmured, his eyes following the high arches. “The carvings match... but pieces are missing. It’s like looking at a shattered puzzle.”

Mina stepped closer, her sharp eyes scanning the stone with intense focus. “These figures are definitely the Sent Ones,” she noted, pointing to the hooded carvings. “And those broken lines look like the Unbound. But these outer borders”—her fingers traced an intricate, swirling design—“the style is completely different. There was another power involved here.”

As she spoke, a recessed section of the wall, half-swallowed by shadow, caught her eye. Mina brushed away centuries of dust and dry moss, revealing a massive, sweeping panorama. The carving depicted a colossal mountain—a towering, jagged peak flanked by slender figures in graceful ceremonial circles. Their faces were carved in reverent postures, with unmistakable pointed ears and flowing hair. The mountain dominated the stone, rendered in staggering detail, its sharp cliffs radiating ancient authority.

“Look at this mountain,” Mina whispered, her voice laced with awe. “That’s not a dwarven peak. That’s the Guardian.”

The party crowded around the exposed relief. The jagged shape of the carved peak matched the ancient legends of the Guardian—the sacred mountain in the South Lands revered in elven myth as a bulwark against ancient ruin. It was a place of legendary power, guarded by the forest tribes, yet its presence here in the deep stone of a dwarven stronghold was an astonishing discovery.

Torgar stepped forward, his heavy boots crushing loose gravel. His dark eyes widened as he studied the elven figures. “The Guardian... the southern elves worship that peak. Their songs say it stands as a shield against the ancient horrors of the world. To them, it is holy ground.”

The group exchanged stunned glances. The connection between the elven holy mountain and the dwarven vaults had never been mentioned in the cult's teachings.

“Did the elves bring these relics to the dwarves?” Lucas asked, his mind piecing the clues together. If the artifacts were tied to the Guardian, then the elves of Haliriel were far more entangled in this war than they let on.

Torgar stroked his braided beard, his expression darkening. “It fits the old tales. The southern tribes had trade routes through these mountains before the Great Wipe. It’s possible their shamans hid the relics in this vault for safekeeping. If these bands were forged for the Guardian, they were made to protect, not destroy.”

As the revelation sank in, Lucas’s thoughts snapped back to their immediate reality. Ancient legends offered no defense against an active pursuit. “Torgar, does the city have anywhere we can study this metal? A workshop or a lab with the right tools to examine magi-tech?”

Torgar shook his head with grim finality. “The Sent Ones only have our study rooms in the Bastion. Dwarves work with hammer and forge. We don't have facilities like the ones in the capital.”

Lucas’s jaw clenched. Without proper instruments or a controlled space to examine the relics, they were flying blind into a storm.

The dwarven council representative, who had remained silent behind the escort, stepped forward. His heavy iron badges glinted in the torchlight. “Lucas,” the official stated plainly. “If you need a proper workshop to study those artifacts, the council can provide one. I will see to it personally.”

Lucas turned to the representative, giving a curt nod. “Get it ready as soon as you can. We can't make a move until we know what's locked onto our skin.”

The group cast a final glance at the ancient murals. The stone walls retained their secrets, but the terrifying shape of the puzzle was beginning to emerge. The artifacts, the elves, and the apocalyptic Disciples were converging on a singular, catastrophic vector.

The return march to the Cult of the Sent Ones’ primary headquarters was thick with suffocating tension. The flickering lanterns lining the stone-tiered thoroughfares did little to ease the heavy dread settling over the city. Lucas walked in absolute silence, his mind processing the fragmented elven reliefs and the chilling certainty of the prophecy. Mina moved at his side, her untamed heat held under strict lockdown as she analyzed the geopolitical fallout of the Guardian relief. Thomas maintained his monolithic pace, masking the intense, throbbing pressure in his skull behind an unyielding expression. Flanking the rear, Dira and Torgar scanned the intersecting alleys with drawn steel, acutely aware that the city’s fragile peace was disintegrating.

As the party breached the inner gates of the Resonant Bastion, a stern-faced dwarven council representative intercepted their path. His long beard was woven with the silver clasps of high diplomacy, and his sharp, dark eyes glinted with an unprecedented urgency.

“Lucas,” the council representative said, stepping forward with urgent gravity. “An urgent dispatch just arrived at the gates. The Elven Citadel of Haliriel is demanding an emergency meeting. Sent directly through our High Council.”

A sharp murmur ran through the gathered cultists. The Citadel of Haliriel was famous across the continent for its fierce isolation. For the High Elves to break centuries of silence during a city siege was a stunning turn of events.

“What do they want?” Lucas asked, his voice sharp and focused.

The council representative shifted his stance, visibly uneasy. “Their message mentions the prophecy of our mountain. They know about the storm that tore through Kingston, and they know about the three relics you took from the vault. I don't know how they got that information, but they demand to speak with you immediately.”

Mina’s green eyes narrowed. “Why now? They stayed quiet while the World Police chased us across the continent. What made them step forward?”

“I don't know,” the representative admitted. “Only that their patience is wearing thin.”

A heavy silence clamped down upon the hall. The elves of Haliriel had always been ghosts on the edge of the map. Their ties to the ancient Guardian had been whispered in legends, but never proven. Now, they were stepping into the open with undeniable urgency.

The silence was broken by the sharp clatter of armored boots as a dwarven messenger pushed through the crowd, carrying a thick parchment scroll sealed with the crimson wax of the royal crest. He handed the scroll to the representative, who broke the seal and scanned the lines. His stoic face tightened.

“The High Elves want the meeting within three days,” the representative announced, rolling the parchment shut. “They insist on meeting at a neutral location outside the mountain, if we refuse to enter their Citadel.”

Lucas felt his pulse quicken. *A neutral location.* That meant something. The elves had zero trust for the cult, and they viewed the dwarven council with equal suspicion. Demanding an open site meant they were preparing for something far bigger than polite diplomacy.

Lucas looked at his companions. Thomas stood like an immovable wall, though the lingering pain in his head tightened his jaw. Mina was tense, already calculating the danger of an open-air meeting. Dira watched with wide, anxious eyes, while Torgar stood lost in thought.

“We’ll meet them,” Lucas said, cutting through the hesitation. “We need to know what they know. We can't afford to walk into this blind.”

The council representative gave a respectful nod. “I will send word immediately. The meeting will be arranged. But there is one more thing.” He paused, glancing at the metal bands locked to their wrists and ankle. “Regarding the workshop you asked for. The council has cleared an advanced magi-tech laboratory in the upper tier. It's being prepped and secured for you right now.”

Lucas nodded. “Good. We need that lab ready before we meet the elves. We have to understand what these relics can do before we talk to them.”

“The lab will be ready, Lucas,” the representative promised, bowing his head. “I will bring you the keys the moment it’s cleared. Until then, the council guarantees your safety within these walls.”

With a final, formal salute, the dwarven official turned and marched out of the Bastion, leaving the party standing in the cavernous hall. The path forward had been violently redrawn. The High Elves of Haliriel had entered the board, carrying the missing pieces of a cosmic puzzle that spanned seventeen centuries.

The parley was inevitable. Every step they took drew them closer to the answers they desperately required—and closer to the heart of an apocalyptic tempest that threatened to erase their world from the timeline entirely.

Glossary of Hybris

Database synchronized. Current indexing: RC1 — Volume I, Chapters 1-16. Arcane Mechanics, Biogenetical Anomalies, Causal Hardware, and Geopolitical Vectors.

Term / Entity Classified Description / Context
Abyss Walkers (Mermaids) Feral, aquatic hominids inhabiting the depths of the Giant Lake. Bipedal predators covered in iridescent scales, featuring dead black eyes adapted for absolute darkness and unhinging jaws filled with translucent, jagged teeth. Driven by primal biological hunger.
Acoustic Void (The Iron Anchor) The biological and thermodynamic manifestation of Thomas. He possesses zero arcane static and absolute immunity to magical frequencies. His musculoskeletal frame acts as an unyielding anchor of pure terrestrial physics, grounding the volatility of his allies.
Aetheric Dam A localized, defensive countermeasure used by the World Police. By artificially spiking the grid's magical density, it creates a hyper-compressed wall of static energy designed to violently overload the friction drives of any breaching magi-tech vehicle.
Aetheric Energy Grid The primary terrestrial power infrastructure of the planet Hybris. Highly susceptible to volatile disruptions from raw magical interference, thermodynamic overload, and arcane tempests.
Arcane Storm A catastrophic, high-yield atmospheric anomaly. Seventeen years ago, one such storm obliterated a Kingston hospital, serving as the violent thermodynamic crucible that facilitated the miraculous survival and arcane saturation of Lucas and Mina.
Blood-rot Berries Highly toxic, darkly swelling flora native to the deep southern jungles. Capable of melting a hunter's throat; a brutal testament to the jungle's lethal adaptability. The plant propagates by feeding on the decomposing mass of the host it kills.
Brum'korath A colossal dwarven stronghold carved into the Storm Mountains. A rigid, isolationist monolith ruled by a secular council and heavily policed by an armored terrestrial militia.
Central Institute An elite educational fortress of magi-tech and arcane physics located in Kingston. It operates mathematically as a panopticon—designed to observe, measure, and dissect prodigies.
Ceylan (The Broken Oracle) An ancient, frail, non-Nythari figure residing in the lightless caves of The Watcher. His mind is unraveling, haunted by fractured, terrifying memories and cosmic mechanics regarding the Children of Hybris.
Cleya / Cleyans An off-world humanoid origin. Characterized by bioluminescent, tendril-like hair that pulses with their emotional state, and a natural, biological affinity for raw thermal output and localized combustion (e.g., Commandant Erika).
Cult of the Sent Ones A dwarven religious order based in Brum'korath. Their belief system is not based on a mythological cycle, but on ancient fragmented Nythari runic tablets detailing a specific historical breach and the second coming of saviors. Driven into absolute chaos after the terrestrial militia breached their subterranean cathedral.
Cult of the Unbound A radical, rival faction operating in the shadows of the Dwarven Lands. They actively utilize deep-cover spies and lethal mercenaries to sabotage the Sent Ones and eliminate the Children of Hybris.
Dark Water Raw, unfiltered dark matter leaking from the shores of the River of Time. It bleeds into the terrestrial atmosphere seeking a vessel when the causal fabric breaks down under extreme arcane pressure.
Dead Zone A localized sector entirely devoid of the aetheric grid. The atmospheric stagnation renders standard magi-tech inoperable and effectively masks thermodynamic and arcane signatures from World Police sensor sweeps.
Dereks (Mountain Dwarves) Hermits of the high peaks of the Storm Mountains. Characterized by incredibly dense, ashen-gray skin that provides natural camouflage and resistance to kinetic impact. They reject advanced magi-tech, relying instead on brutal, raw earth and water magic.
Dira A dwarven guide who infiltrated the Cult of the Sent Ones. Revealed through Lucas's telepathic intrusion to be a deep-cover spy orchestrated by the Cult of the Unbound.
Disciples Living weapons of mass devastation prophesied to pave the way for the Central Galactic Empire's return. Their descent is mathematically triggered by catastrophic ruptures of raw energy, acting as lethal heralds of the second coming.
Durnak & Grimbar Vanguards of the Sent Ones under Torgar. Grimbar's cognitive matrix was aggressively bypassed by Lucas, exposing his treason as an operative for the Unbound. Durnak remains a loyal, grounded defender of the Bastion.
Elder Valka & Elder Gorla Presiding dwarven elders of the secular magistrate in Brum'korath. They conducted the political tribunal following the aqueduct breach, seeking to balance civic stability against the militarized fanaticism of the Unbound.
Elias Thorne / The Lead Researcher The cold, calculating architect of Lucas’s childhood containment in the medi-laboratories. He views human trauma, atomic manipulation, and arcane physics purely as harvestable empirical data.
Giant Lake A colossal geographical anomaly separating the Storm Mountains from the Central Lands. It acts as a massive thermal sink and is prone to sudden, violent thermodynamic collapses. Guarded by World Police perimeter outposts and apex aquatic predators.
Goldar Ironfist High Cleric of the Cult of the Sent Ones. A towering figure of authority whose reign ended when he was captured by the terrestrial militia during the siege of the subterranean cathedral in Brum'korath.
Goldar's Trial & Secular Council The emergency judicial tribunal convened in the Halls of Justice following the catastrophic titan incursion. High Cleric Goldar was stripped of clerical jurisdiction, while the Council established a fragile tactical truce with the Children of Hybris to examine the deep vaults.
Haliriel (The Elven Citadel) A breathtaking architectural marvel blending pale stone and living Serran trees. The city operates in a strict caste system: the chaotic Outsider District (Market) at the base, the lavish Second District requiring biometric writs, and the absolute apex, the Third District, housing the High Temple of Nature.
High Elves Council The ruling body of Haliriel, operating from the High Temple of Nature in the Third District. Composed of ancient elites, including Queen Aphyrosia, who govern with an overwhelming, silent authority and strict adherence to the prophecy.
High Elven Parley (Citadel of Haliriel) An unprecedented diplomatic summons transmitted by the elven leadership of Haliriel directly to the High Council of Brum'korath. Bypassing centuries of isolationism, the dispatch demanded an emergency summit at a neutral terrestrial coordinate outside the mountain.
Hybris The terrestrial planet where the primary narrative is anchored. Marked by stark landscapes, dormant magic, and oppressive structural governance.
Intracranial Overwrite (Thomas's Neural Restructuring) A violent cognitive reconfiguration triggered when Thomas bonded with his relic. Because his biology operates as an absolute non-magical bedrock, the causal hardware bypassed standard arcane channels, embedding directly into his neural matrix and initiating an autonomous algorithmic restructuring of his thoughts.
Invisible Steps Protocol A localized kinetic suppression algorithm. It forces Mina to mathematically bleed her extreme kinetic exhaust safely into the earth's mass, preventing atmospheric shockwaves and lethal systemic scrutiny.
Kinetic Delta / Organic Momentum The terrifying, untamed creation energy pooling in Mina's blood. When the psychological brakes slip, her velocity transcends terrestrial thermodynamics, displacing matter and fracturing fluid dynamics into localized tsunamis or atmospheric vacuums.
Krin Dow-Kabar A grounded, pragmatic dwarven merchant. Rescued by the party's kinetic and atomic intervention, he provided them bypass access through the heavily fortified gates of Brum'korath.
Lucas's Synthesis Mind / Atomic Volatility Lucas's cognitive survival mechanism forged in the absolute isolation of the medi-laboratory. It processes emotional trauma, social friction, and raw reality through hyper-accelerated quantum calculus and thermodynamic threat assessments.
Magi-Tech A synthesized engineering discipline blending archaic magical frequencies with high-end technological mechanics (e.g., Lumishards, hover-pods, aetheric rails, biometric sentinels).
Nefris & Vardis Planets located in the peripheral orbital grid during the future Timeline-A5 war. Nefris is a war-torn Imperial meat grinder. Vardis is a dense, heavily patrolled jungle world serving as the hazardous drop zone for the Starlight Voyager.
Nythari (Candice, Jarek, Elder Aria) Fiercely territorial, wilderness-adapted tribes descended from the First Ancestors. They survived ancient purges by bleeding their existence into the roots of the deep southern jungles. Their fragmented oral histories and runic records secretly form the foundation of the Dwarven prophecy.
Relics of Timeline-0 / Causal Hardware (Biometric Lock) Hyper-advanced metallic artifacts forged near the End of Time by the founders of Timeline-0. Engineered as biometric safety valves to regulate raw magical volatility, they bind seamlessly to host biology. When bonded to Lucas-A, the relic flagged a 0.0001% biogenetic variance, locking out master-level functionality.
Resonant Bastion The subterranean headquarters and inner sanctum of the Cult of the Sent Ones within Brum'korath. A massive, vaulted labyrinth equipped with cavernous auditory halls, training rings, and ancient archives.
Serran Trees Towering arboreal giants native to both the deep southern jungle and the architecture of Haliriel. Their structures are fortified by millennia of dormant magic.
Sleepwalking Carnage An autonomous, subconscious biometric defense mechanism. Triggered by extreme arcane resonance between Lucas and Mina, it overrides conscious restraints, violently discharging their suppressed atomic and kinetic exhaust into the atmosphere.
Stone's Hollow A lightless, subterranean stronghold beneath Brum'korath acting as the operational epicenter for the Cult of the Unbound.
Sub-dermal Resonance Tracker A covert, aetheric hardware chip embedded below Lucas’s collarbone by Elias Thorne. It broadcasts a precise biological and magical resonance frequency, allowing authorities to trace his trajectory. Extracted and pulverized by Thomas.
The Broken Messiah (Lucas-A5) A future iteration of Lucas glimpsed in the 1775 HSC timeline. His synthesis mind is fractured into a million jagged pieces by arcane exhaustion and trauma. Transported under heavy iron restraints by John and Erika.
The Guardian Peak Relief A colossal subterranean mural discovered in the deep vaults of Brum'korath, depicting deep-forest elves in worshipful posture around the sacred Guardian mountain. It mathematically links the dwarven relics to the ancient southern elven defense grid.
The Lupine Anomaly (The Minulican) A multidimensional byproduct forged from the violent thermodynamic collision of Lucas and Mina’s raw magic in the Kingston Square. A hulking, demonic mass of flesh, bone, and violet lightning acting as an uncontrolled cosmic variable.
The Uncle & Wallace Mina’s adoptive handlers operating from a gilded Kingston estate. The Uncle wields immense wealth and calculated pride, while Wallace serves as an unyielding, tactical sentinel and discreet bodyguard (Logistical Interventionist).
The Watcher An isolated, jagged peak south of the western continent. It acts as an ancient arcane epicenter and an archival tombstone for a world that has forgotten its own history.
Thermal Shock Equation An emergency thermodynamic calculation executed by Lucas during the Disciple of Earth siege. By superheating the titan's silicate armor to critical mass and flashing it with municipal aqueduct water, the resulting thermal contraction shattered the monster's impenetrable mantle into brittle glass.
Thrainor Blackstone The ruthless architect of the Cult of the Unbound. He orchestrated the infiltration of the Sent Ones, utilizing operatives like Dira and Grimbar to systematically fracture their perimeter.
Torgar A dwarven cleric within the Cult of the Sent Ones. Stern, unrelenting, and adorned in deep burgundy robes. He advocated for rigid meditative control over Lucas's atomic friction prior to the fall of their sanctuary.
Tredmor The chaotic, outer settlement sprawling beneath the massive iron gates of Brum'korath. Functions as a punishing atmospheric bottleneck where merchants, mercenaries, and outcasts bleed their physical momentum.
World Police / Terrestrial Hegemony The global law enforcement apparatus controlling the Central Lands. A heavily militarized, bureaucratic machine that sweeps the aetheric grid to hunt, catalog, and eliminate unregistered biological anomalies.

Appendices

System Archive: Temporal and Causal Measurements.

The Hybris Standard Calendar (HSC)

Established Year 0 HSC by the Founders' Scientific Council following the arrival of the exiled.
Current Year: 1772 HSC

Year Structure

  • The year consists of 10 Months.
  • Each Month consists of 3 Weeks.
  • Each Week consists of 10 Days.
  • Each Day consists of 24 Hours.

(Total Days per Month: 30  |  Total Days per Year: 300)

Month Names

Named after prominent scientists and researchers from the founding council.

  1. Aris: (Perhaps after Ariston, a logician/physicist)
  2. Borin: (Maybe Borlund, a geologist/resource analyst)
  3. Cygnus: (Likely named by an astronomer/navigator)
  4. Delia: (Possibly Delianova, a biologist/xenobotanist)
  5. Elara: (Could be Elarian, a historian/archivist, also a character name)
  6. Feron: (Maybe Feronus, a chemist/materials scientist)
  7. Galen: (After Galenus, likely a physician/medic)
  8. Heston: (Perhaps Hestonius, an engineer/architect)
  9. Ilias: (Could be Iliadra, a linguist/communications expert, also similar to Elias)
  10. Jorvan: (Maybe Jorvanis, a sociologist/political theorist)

Week Structure & Day Naming

Weeks are identified by suffixes related to the phases of Hybris's most prominent moon (or a conceptual cycle if no moon). There are 10 base Day Names that cycle through the weeks, suggesting names that evoke order or mathematical cycles.

  • Solus: (Meaning 'alone' or 'first')
  • Duon: (Related to 'two')
  • Trion: (Related to 'three')
  • Quadra: (Related to 'four')
  • Penta: (Related to 'five')
  • Hexa: (Related to 'six')
  • Septa: (Related to 'seven')
  • Octa: (Related to 'eight')
  • Nova: (Meaning 'new', perhaps ninth)
  • Deca: (Related to 'ten' or 'completion')

Week Suffixes (Moon Cycle Concept)

  • Week 1 Suffix: -cres (Representing the Crescent or waxing/growing phase)
  • Week 2 Suffix: -plen (Representing the Plena or full/peak phase)
  • Week 3 Suffix: -wan (Representing the Waning or decreasing phase)

Example Output

If an event occurred on the 5th day of the 2nd week of the 7th month in the year 1772, it is recorded as:

Penta-plen, Galen 1772 HSC
